all_shares_card_description_empty: Everyone's uploaded shares, including anonymous ones. Retrieval codes are not shown here.
all_shares_card_description_total: {total} total. Retrieval codes are not shown here.
all_shares_delete_dialog_description: The link becomes invalid immediately, even for someone who already has the retrieval code. Files are removed later by background cleanup — this can't be undone.
dashboard_config_description: Determined at startup by environment variables or the config file — this page is view-only
dashboard_config_readonly_badge: Read-only · requires a config change and service restart
dashboard_stats_available_invites_sub: Not yet used up or expired
dashboard_storage_trend_description: Storage used over the past 7 days
home_description: The default locale is set to Traditional Chinese.
home_subtitle: This admin interface uses the shared i18n package.
invites_card_description: Whether a code is still usable is decided by the server, not calculated locally from its count and time.
roles_byte_limit_inherit_description: {inheritLabel} — follows whenever the site-wide setting changes
roles_byte_limit_unlimited_description: This role doesn't apply its own limit
roles_card_description: Permissions are a fixed list decided by the program; roles are what can be added or removed. Built-in roles can't be deleted or have their permissions changed.
roles_delete_dialog_description_empty: This role currently has no members.
roles_delete_dialog_description_with_mem: There are currently {members} accounts in this role. After deletion they'll be left without a role — able to sign in, but unable to do anything.
roles_editor_blocked_warning: This role has permissions you don't hold yourself (
roles_editor_description_custom: Permissions are submitted as a full set, not just the changed part.
roles_editor_description_system: A built-in role's name and quota can be changed, but not its permissions — to reduce what an ordinary account can do, create a role of your own instead.
roles_editor_permissions_system_note: This is a built-in role — its permissions can't be changed.
settings_account_description: Who can register, what role new accounts get, and how long sign-in sessions and logs are retained
settings_account_form_default_role_descr: The role assigned when registration completes, corresponding to auth.default_role.
settings_account_form_login_history_desc: How many days an ended session stays in the login history, 90 days by default. Its purpose is answering "did someone else get in," so it outlives the credential itself.
settings_account_form_registration_descr: This also governs third-party sign-in: once registration is closed, OIDC/GitHub/Discord sign-in only works for people who already have an account — new people are rejected. An administrator can still create accounts manually after it's closed.
settings_account_form_roles_error: (Role list failed to load — only the current value can be kept)
settings_account_form_session_ttl_descri: How long after signing in a user needs to sign in again, 720 hours (30 days) by default.
settings_appearance_form_accent_descript: The accent color for buttons, links, and the focus ring. Each color is a block of CSS in packages/ui, so only these seven are available.
settings_appearance_form_mode_descriptio: The light/dark setting applied on a guest's first visit; they can still switch it themselves afterward. "Follow device" reads prefers-color-scheme.
settings_appearance_form_theme_cosmic_de: A deep blue-violet night sky, best in dark mode.
settings_appearance_form_theme_descripti: The neutral palette used for backgrounds, text, and borders.
settings_appearance_form_theme_matsu_des: Warm rice paper with olive green, a soft hand-drawn tone.
settings_appearance_form_theme_sepia_des: Warm as paper, comfortable for long reading.
settings_appearance_form_theme_slate_des: A clean, cool gray that stays out of the content's way.
settings_appearance_form_theme_vintage_d: Low-contrast tea-stained paper, like old print.
settings_appearance_preview_card_descrip: Guests will see this color scheme until they choose one themselves.
settings_auth_providers_discord_descript: Discord is likewise not an OIDC provider. There's no self-hosted version, so there's no custom domain to configure.
settings_auth_providers_discord_scopes_h: Space-separated. Without email, Discord won't provide an email address, and every sign-in will fail with no_address.
settings_auth_providers_github_base_url_: For GitHub Enterprise Server (self-hosted on your own domain). Leave blank for github.com.
settings_auth_providers_github_descripti: GitHub is not an OIDC provider (it doesn't issue an id_token) — its endpoints are hardcoded in the adapter, so the only values here are the ones that identify this site to GitHub.
settings_auth_providers_github_scopes_hi: Space-separated. Without user:email, GitHub won't provide a verified email address, and every sign-in will fail with no_address.
settings_feature_form_accounts_descripti: Registration, sign-in, and sessions. Turning it off means no accounts at all, suited to "one person behind a VPN who just wants a file drop point". Deliberately independent of anonymous uploads — wanting an admin panel doesn't mean wanting to force everyone to register.
settings_feature_form_accounts_off_warni: With account features off, no one can sign in, and this panel requires a session to enter — the next reload will lock you out.
settings_feature_form_admin_description: The endpoint this entire admin panel depends on. Turning it off means you can no longer open this screen — the only way back is to set the environment variable TESSERA_FEATURES__ADMIN=true and restart.
settings_feature_form_admin_lockout_desc: Once the admin endpoint is off, every API this screen depends on returns 404, and the panel can't fix itself. The only way to recover is to set
on the server and restart. Only click Save if you're sure you want to do this.
settings_feature_form_admin_lockout_titl: Saving will lock you out of this panel
settings_feature_form_intro: Runtime switches. A feature that's turned off never has its routes mounted at all, so calling it gets a plain 404 — not a 403 that would confirm it exists.
settings_feature_form_og_layout_descript: Leave blank to use the built-in card. Setting it replaces the card for every share. Only
are allowed, and it can't point at resources outside this server — the backend rejects it outright if it does. In a locked share's card,
will be empty — because the value itself is empty, not because the template applies any protection.
settings_features_description: Runtime toggles and custom link preview cards
settings_form_fields_sealed_description_: Currently set. The original value can't be read back here — leave it empty to keep it unchanged, fill it in to overwrite it.
Currently not set. Fill it in and save to take effect; afterwards this field still won't show the original value.
settings_form_fields_sealed_placeholder_: Already set — leave empty to keep unchanged
settings_form_footer_read_only: You can only view these settings — changing them requires the settings:write permission.
settings_guest_warning_account_action: change the default role for new accounts
settings_guest_warning_body_before: New accounts default to "guest" (no permissions), but anonymous uploads are still on — the same person can log out and upload as a stranger anyway. To actually block this, go to
settings_guest_warning_title: The guest role currently restricts no one
settings_mail_description: SMTP relay, sender address, and the expiration time of password reset and registration confirmation links
settings_mail_form_from_description: The mail's From: address. The domain must already be verified with the relay, or the mail will be bounced.
settings_mail_form_host_description: SMTP host. Leave blank to turn off all mail sending.
settings_mail_form_host_empty_warning: Leaving the SMTP host blank means this instance sends no mail at all — password resets and registration confirmations won't work. This field expects a relay (Resend, Brevo, SES, Fastmail, or your own company's) — residential connections can't send mail, most ISPs block port 25, and receiving servers reject residential addresses outright.
settings_mail_form_password_description: Most relays expect an API key here.
settings_mail_form_port_description: 587 is submission + STARTTLS (the default); 465 is implicit TLS, also common.
settings_mail_form_public_url_descriptio: The base URL used for links inside mail. This deliberately uses a configured value rather than the request's Host header — building a reset link from a header that can be spoofed would point it at an attacker's server, handing them the token.
settings_mail_form_registration_ttl_desc: How long a registration confirmation link stays valid, default 24 hours, capped at 168 (7 days). It can be longer because it grants less — clicking it creates an account using the password the applicant already chose themselves.
settings_mail_form_reset_ttl_description: How many minutes a password reset link stays valid, default 30, capped at 1440 (24 hours). It's short because the link itself is a credential — it only needs to outlast the mail queue.
settings_mail_form_username_description: Resend requires the literal string resend here.
settings_network_description: Public-facing URL, trusted reverse proxies, and session cookie and timeout
settings_network_form_always_secure_body: If any segment of the path is plaintext HTTP, the browser will accept the response but drop the cookie — the user sees a successful sign-in, then nothing happens, with no error message anywhere. If unsure, choose "Auto."
settings_network_form_always_secure_titl: Only choose this for a deployment that is HTTPS end-to-end
settings_network_form_cookie_secure_desc: When to mark the session cookie Secure. Auto marks it only over HTTPS, compatible with both a plaintext LAN deployment and a public TLS one.
settings_network_form_public_url_descrip: This site's absolute public URL. Only link previews need it, and it must be absolute — og:image is fetched by a crawler on another machine. Left empty, it's derived from each request's Host, which breaks behind a reverse proxy that rewrites Host, or in a container that only sees localhost. A blank preview card means this needs to be set.
settings_network_form_request_timeout_de: The time budget for regular requests, 30 seconds by default. It doesn't apply to the upload route — a single number can't satisfy both "let a 5GB file trickle in" and "don't let someone who connects and sends nothing hold a slot."
settings_network_form_trusted_proxies_de: One entry per line, CIDR or bare address. For a same-host proxy use 127.0.0.1 and ::1; for a container network use 10.0.0.0/8. Trusting nothing by default is deliberate: X-Forwarded-For is set by whoever talked to us last, so trusting it unconditionally lets the caller pick their own source address — and every throttle below counts against that address.
settings_network_form_upload_stall_descr: How long an upload can go without receiving any bytes before it's considered disconnected, 30 seconds by default. It only asks "is the other side still sending," so a large file is unaffected no matter how long it takes.
settings_oauth_card_client_id_descriptio: This sign-in button only appears once both Client ID and Client Secret are filled in.
settings_oauth_card_display_name_descrip: The text on the sign-in button. Leave it empty to use the provider's name.
settings_oauth_card_link_by_email_descri: Allow this identity to link to an existing account with the same email. Accounts with these two providers can be created in a minute — enabling open registration together with email matching hands other people's accounts away, so this is off by default.
settings_oauth_card_link_by_email_label: Link to an existing account by verified email
settings_oidc_card_description: Set an issuer to enable, clear it to disable. All other endpoints are read from the issuer's discovery document.
settings_oidc_card_display_name_descript: The text on the sign-in button. Leave it empty to use the issuer's domain.
settings_oidc_card_group_claim_descripti: Which claim the groups are in. Authentik/Authelia use groups, Keycloak uses realm_access.roles, some LDAP bridges use memberOf. Use dots to select nested fields.
settings_oidc_card_issuer_description: Must be https, and must match the iss claim the provider puts in the id_token exactly (required by spec). Clearing it disables OIDC sign-in.
settings_oidc_card_link_by_email_descrip: Allow the provider's identity to link to an existing account with the same email. Even when enabled, the provider still has to report email_verified.
settings_oidc_card_link_by_email_label: Link to an existing account by verified email
settings_oidc_card_open_warning_body: Leaving "Required group" empty means no filtering. The provider authenticates anyone who has an account with it — if that's a public service like Google, this is open registration for the entire world. To restrict it, fill in a group name.
settings_oidc_card_open_warning_title: Any account from this provider can currently sign in
settings_oidc_card_required_group_descri: Only members of this group may sign in. Leave it empty to let any account the provider authenticates in.
settings_oidc_card_scopes_description: Space-separated. openid is added automatically if missing; email is required — sign-ins without an email are rejected.
settings_oidc_discovery_field_descriptio: This is usually the URL copied straight from the provider's dashboard. The server reads it, and the Issuer and Scopes it finds are filled in below — you don't need to fill in the endpoints, the backend reads them from the same document at sign-in time. Leave it blank to read the Issuer field's current value instead.
settings_oidc_discovery_field_missing_em: This provider doesn't declare the email scope. Without a verified email address, every sign-in will fail with no_address.
settings_oidc_discovery_field_no_scopes_: The document doesn't declare scopes_supported, so Scopes is left unchanged — not declaring it doesn't mean it isn't supported.
settings_oidc_discovery_field_read_succe: The server read it successfully and filled in the fields below
settings_oidc_discovery_field_supported_: Scopes supported by this provider: {scopes}. The Scopes field below has been aligned to this list.
settings_oidc_discovery_unreadable: Could not read the configuration document at this address.
settings_password_description: Password length rules and Argon2id cost parameters
settings_password_form_argon2_intro_1: The following are Argon2id's cost parameters. Changing these
settings_password_form_argon2_intro_3: — the parameters are stored inside the hash value itself and read from there at verification time, so this only affects newly generated hashes.
settings_password_form_composition_intro: (registration, password change, reset). Sign-in isn't checked, so turning these on
, but they'll need to follow the new rules the next time they change their password. Character categories are judged by Unicode, so passwords in any language are held to the same standard.
settings_password_form_intro_1: Length is the primary rule. Per NIST 800-63B: composition rules only push people toward
settings_password_form_intro_2: and length matters more than the character set, so the three switches below are off by default. They're kept for internal policies that still require composition rules.
settings_password_form_max_length_descri: Capped at 1024. A cap is needed because an unbounded password field lets an unauthenticated request make the server do an unbounded amount of work.
settings_password_form_memory_kib_descri: Default 19456 (19 MiB, the OWASP-recommended value). The most critical parameter — memory cost is what makes GPU cracking expensive, but it also means peak sign-in memory use is multiplied by concurrent executions, so do the math on whether this machine can handle it before raising it.
settings_password_form_min_length_descri: The floor is 8 — it can't go any lower.
settings_password_form_pwned_enabled_des: Checks Have I Been Pwned when a new password is set; passwords found on breach lists are rejected. This server must be able to reach the address below.
settings_password_form_pwned_intro_1: The breached-password check also only applies when choosing a new password. Only the first 5 characters of the password's SHA-1 hash are sent out, with matching done locally (k-anonymity) — the full password and full hash never leave this server. If the service can't be reached (timeout, connection failure, non-200), it
settings_password_form_pwned_intro_3: , leaving only a single log line — registration and password reset shouldn't stall just because someone else's service is down.
settings_password_form_pwned_url_descrip: The range API's address, defaulting to the official service. If you don't want to depend on it, or this server has no internet access, point it at a self-hosted implementation instead.
settings_password_form_require_mixed_cas: Requires both uppercase and lowercase letters.
settings_password_form_require_symbol_de: Requires at least one symbol. Whitespace doesn't count — otherwise any passphrase would pass automatically, making the rule meaningless.
settings_provider_callback_backchannel_h: Optional. Once registered, signing out on the provider's side (or the account being disabled) pushes a logout token here, which ends the session on this side too; without it, the session simply waits to expire on its own.
settings_provider_callback_intro: Register these with the provider's dashboard. If any are missing or mistyped, they'll reject sign-in, and the error will only show up on their page.
settings_provider_callback_no_public_url: The redirect URL is built from

It's not set, there's no address to give you here, and third-party sign-in itself will also fail — the backend has no address to tell the provider to redirect back to. Please fill it in under "Network".
Set the public URL first to know what to register
settings_provider_callback_redirect_hint: OAuth dashboards usually call this Redirect URI, Callback URL, or Redirect URL.
settings_provider_registration_detail_cl: Registration is off, so anyone without an existing account here will be rejected when signing in, seeing "registration is closed." People already linked, or matched to an existing account by the same verified email, are unaffected.
settings_provider_registration_detail_in: New users without an invite code will be rejected. The invite code must be attached to the sign-in link (`/login?invite=code`) — being authenticated by the provider doesn't mean being accepted here.
settings_provider_registration_detail_op: Anyone who can be authenticated by this provider gets a new account. If it's a public service (like Google), this is open registration for the entire world.
settings_provider_registration_headline_: Only existing accounts can currently use third-party sign-in
Third-party sign-in currently requires an invite code to open a new account
Third-party sign-in currently opens a new account for anyone automatically
settings_schema_absolute_url: Must be an absolute URL starting with http(s)://
settings_schema_access_log_retention_min: When access logging is enabled, retention must be at least 1 day (there is no "keep forever" value)
settings_schema_expiry_order: Default retention cannot exceed the maximum retention
settings_schema_mail_from_required: Please enter a complete sender address
settings_schema_mail_trio_incomplete: SMTP host, sender address, and mail link base URL must be either all filled in or all left empty
settings_schema_min_part_size: Must be at least 5 MiB (S3's minimum part size)
settings_schema_oidc_issuer_https: Must be an issuer URL starting with https://
settings_schema_oidc_issuer_not_discover: This is a discovery URL, not an issuer. Paste it into the field above and click "Read & fill in" — the issuer will be read from the document
settings_schema_password_length_order: Minimum length cannot exceed maximum length
settings_schema_pwned_url_required: Must be an absolute URL starting with http(s):// when enabled
settings_schema_throttle_attempts_floor: At least 1 attempt — 0 locks everyone out
settings_schema_throttle_window_floor: At least 1 second — 0 disables the limit entirely
settings_share_description: Retrieval codes, download authorization lifetime, cleanup, and retrieval logs
settings_share_form_access_log_enabled_d: Whether to log every retrieval individually. Off by default, deliberately — view_count is just an integer that says nothing about where a visitor was, while an access log entry is an address plus a browser string, recording someone who merely received a link and agreed to nothing.
settings_share_form_access_log_notice_1: Once enabled, this instance will keep visitors' addresses and browser strings.
settings_share_form_access_log_notice_2: An instance that enables this should disclose it on the page.
settings_share_form_access_log_retention: How many days to retain the log, default 30. When enabled, it can't be 0 — reading 0 as "forever" would be the wrong default for a setting about other people's data, so the backend rejects it outright.
settings_share_form_code_length_descript: The number of characters in the retrieval code, default 8. Eight Crockford base32 characters give about 1.1×10¹² combinations; some similar services use 5 characters, only 33 million, which a public endpoint could exhaustively walk through. A short code only holds up as long as the rate limit on the "retrieval code lookup" endpoint exists.
settings_share_form_inline_threshold_des: Anything smaller than this is stored in the database rather than object storage, default 64 KiB. Most shares are short notes or code snippets, where a round trip to object storage costs more than the space it saves — as a side benefit, database backups then cover the content too.
settings_share_form_max_text_bytes_descr: The size limit for plain-text shares, default 1 MiB. Text is stored in the database, so this is both the maximum size of a single row and the maximum memory a single upload can occupy — the whole thing is received at once and can't be streamed.
settings_share_form_retain_after_death_d: How long a share is kept after it expires or is used up before actually being deleted, default 168 (7 days); 0 means it's deleted on the next cleanup. Keeping it around lets the link say "this has expired" rather than "code not found" — only the former is worth asking for again.
settings_share_form_ticket_idle_descript: How long a ticket can sit idle before expiring, default 1 hour, pushed back on every use. Idle-based rather than a fixed lifetime: a ticket is just a string and so can be forwarded, and a fixed lifetime would need to cover "the slowest connection downloading the largest file" — a ticket that lives that long becomes worth forwarding.
settings_share_form_ticket_ttl_descripti: The maximum lifetime of a download authorization, default 24 hours. One authorization consumes one retrieval count; the ticket it produces afterward can be reused (Range requests, resuming, retrying after a disconnect) — without this separation, a single interrupted download would burn through a one-time share. This is a ceiling, not the typical case.
settings_share_form_upload_session_ttl_d: How long an incomplete upload is kept, default 24 hours. During that time, its bytes still count against the quota. Long enough that a laptop closed overnight can still resume, short enough that dead sessions don't pile up. If you use S3, also set a separate AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload rule with a few more days than this.
settings_site_description: Browser tab title and link preview, maps to site.*
settings_site_form_description_descripti: The description shown in the preview card when someone shares a link to this site itself. Leave it blank to omit this meta tag. Up to {max} characters.
settings_site_form_title_description: The page title, also used as the site name in link previews. Can't be blank, up to {max} characters.
settings_storage_description: Storage backend address and multipart upload chunk size
settings_storage_form_part_size_descript: How much data accumulates before a part is sent. S3 rejects any part smaller than 5 MiB except the last one; Cloudflare R2 additionally requires every part to be the same size, so on R2 this value should equal the minimum.
settings_storage_form_url_description_1: Where blobs are stored. The URL carries credentials (
settings_storage_form_url_description_2: ), so the panel can neither read nor write it — it can only be set with the environment variable
settings_theme_description: The default appearance visitors see, maps to appearance.*
settings_theme_field_description: The theme setting is saved only for the current user.
settings_throttle_description: Six counters, each protecting a different resource
settings_throttle_form_intro: Six counters protect different things, so they're set separately. Neither value can be 0: 0 attempts locks everyone out (the entire machine, for "Total source address"), while a 0-second window never blocks anything — it looks on but is actually off. To loosen a limit, raise the attempt count, not the window to 0.
settings_throttle_form_lookup_protects: Lookups of pickup codes that don't exist. Short pickup codes rely entirely on this group for safety — loosening it lets someone walk the entire pickup code space.
settings_throttle_form_max_tracked_keys_: The maximum number of keys tracked before a sweep, shared across all six groups. This is a memory cap, not a security setting: each key is a string chosen by an unauthenticated stranger, and this number decides how much memory they can make the process hold. Capped at 100000.
settings_throttle_form_share_protects: Wrong guesses of a share's password.
settings_throttle_form_source_protects: Any expensive operation. Deliberately lenient — addresses are shared, so blocking one blocks everyone behind it too.
settings_upload_description: Upload rate limiting, size limits, and retention period
settings_upload_form_allow_anonymous_des: When off, only signed-in accounts can upload, corresponding to features.anonymous_upload.
settings_upload_form_default_expiry_desc: The default retention used when an upload doesn't specify one; 0 falls back to the max retention below. This affects disk usage more than any quota.
settings_upload_form_max_body_descriptio: Maximum request body size. Changing it here only takes half effect — the check in the upload path reads the current setting, but the gatekeeping middleware is baked in when routes are built, so it can only be changed via the environment variable
settings_upload_form_max_expiry_descript: The longest retention a user may request; 0 means no cap.
settings_upload_form_max_total_bytes_des: The total content limit for the whole instance, 0 means unlimited. Leaving it unset while guest uploads are on turns this into an unlimited network drive open to anyone who can reach it, and the first sign of trouble is a full disk.
settings_upload_form_throttle_attempts_d: How many expensive operations the same source can make within the window. Can't be 0 — 0 attempts locks out the entire machine, so the server refuses to start with that value.
settings_upload_form_throttle_window_des: The window length counted by source address, corresponding to auth.throttle.source.window_secs. This one is deliberately lenient — addresses are shared, so blocking one blocks everyone behind it too.
users_action_delete_description: The account will be reduced to a "Deleted account" row — this can't be undone. Their uploaded shares are not deleted with it; they become anonymous shares and stay active. Use "End all shares" separately to clear those.
users_action_disable_description: They'll be signed out immediately and won't be able to sign in again; their API tokens are invalidated at the same time. Their shares still work for recipients. You can re-enable this account at any time.
users_action_last_admin_error: This is the last account that can grant permissions — hand that permission to someone else first.
users_action_remove_shares_description: Every share this account uploaded becomes invalid immediately, and any links already handed out stop working too — this can't be undone. The account itself is unaffected.
users_card_description: "Unassigned" means nobody has decided what this account can do yet — that's different from deliberately giving it the guest role.
users_set_role_dialog_description: An account has at most one role. Choosing "Unassigned" means the account can sign in but can't do anything.
